basics.name: Robert DeRose
basics.label: Systems & Platform Engineering | Embedded Linux & IoT
basics.summary:
I build software that bridges hardware and the cloud: embedded Linux, IoT device management, mesh messaging, and the CI/CD to ship it. Shipping code since 2010 in Python, Java, Elixir, Go, Rust, TypeScript, and Nix: the right tool for each job.

For 3 years I've been the lead engineer for SFERO, Checkpoint's best-selling new product, with large deployments worldwide, and for the CI/CD the whole company ships on. Since 2025 I've worked agent-first with models from Anthropic and OpenAI, using spec-driven development and Beads. Working this way, I made a ~64K-line custom DDS messaging prototype unnecessary by packaging Zenoh with an MQTT bridge in ~2 weeks.

work.name: Checkpoint Systems
work.summary: Lead engineer for SFERO, Checkpoint's best-selling new product, since 2023, with large deployments worldwide.
highlights: Replaced a multicast-based, ~64K-line custom DDS messaging prototype (5 months of work) with a packaged Zenoh/MQTT platform in ~2 weeks, adding mutual TLS (mTLS) across the device fleet, per-application leader election, and a React operator console

Rewrote every device UI as React 19 and PatternFly 6 modules on Vite with custom mise tooling, consolidated overlapping Cockpit modules, and shipped a customized Cockpit build with Entra ID sign-in, removing ~77K lines of legacy code

Rebuilt the provisioning app in Rust/Tauri, used by every approved employee and contractor: an Entra ID-secured server supplies the device credentials, which stay in the macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager

Introduced spec-driven development with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex), Beads for task tracking, and gated code review across the team's repositories, taking the team from small agent tasks to whole projects
As a spare-time side project, prototyped an Elixir/OTP successor to the RFID loss-prevention platform, with restart-safe alarm processing and alarm strategies operators can change without new code

Established the company's packaging and release standard: shared CI/CD on reusable GitHub Actions and a spec-tested Bash framework that builds Debian packages for Python, Rust, and TypeScript on arm64 and amd64, adopted by 30+ repositories in 3 offices
Built a self-hosted GitHub Actions platform on ephemeral runners: builds are 10x faster and reproducible, with no leftovers from other pipelines
Rebuilt the APT repository server around filesystem watchers and a cached index: packages publish in under a minute instead of hours
Redesigned the device OS packages around Linux standards instead of home-grown conventions, removing ~44K lines of legacy code, and led EN 18031 hardening
Strengthened device security by replacing custom privilege handling with sudo rules, polkit, and Cockpit's native APIs, and added Entra ID sign-in (OIDC) with role-based access to the device UIs
Built a generic GPIO REST service for CPU GPIO and latched or unlatched I2C expanders; a YAML file is all a new device needs
Led the Python service that provisions, monitors, and updates networked RFID and EAS readers, adding three hardware families and over-the-air firmware updates over MQTT
Created the Copier templates new projects start from, with the shared CI/CD, packaging, and UI tooling built in, including the REST service base behind Checkpoint's Readfinity Core reader software

work.name: Edmunds GovTech
highlights: Built an automated upgrade system that took government customers straight from several major versions behind to the latest release, saving technicians hours to days per upgrade
Designed its database migration engine for MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and Actian Zen (PSQL), replacing years of schema changes tracked by hand in Excel
Led a team of three developers integrating Orbeon Forms into the product
Migrated all source code from Subversion to Git and set up GitLab CI/CD

work.name: Linode, Inc.
highlights: Built Linode's OAuth 2.0 platform across the legacy ColdFusion site and the new Python API: single sign-on for Linode's apps, an OAuth provider for third-party apps, and an SSH PAM module for console login with optional 2FA

Built reproducible local development environments, first with Vagrant and SaltStack, then Docker Compose, so anyone in the company could contribute; one support engineer who started this way became one of the team's best developers
Championed and implemented the OpenAPI 3 specification for Linode API v4

work.name: Mitel (formerly Ulticom, Inc.)
highlights: Developed a distributed, fault-tolerant Diameter Signaling Controller on Cisco's NCS platform, with SOAP and REST APIs (Apache CXF, Jersey) and a metrics system for observability

work.name: Amazon.com
highlights: Developed an IP reputation system and email deliverability monitoring for Amazon Simple Email Service (SES), tracking how mail providers treated Amazon's mail servers

projects.name: Nixstasis
projects.description: Self-hosted IoT fleet monitoring and remote device access, no inbound ports.
highlights: Contract-enforced client/server E2E test harness
Remote SSH through lease-bound tunnel credentials, a sandboxed Starlark scripting system, and command allowlist policies
Releases ship .deb, .rpm, and .run packages and container images from CI, with a Docusaurus site for docs and product pages

projects.name: AtomixOS
projects.description: NixOS for single-board computers with atomic A/B system updates and automatic rollback.
highlights: Signed RAUC bundles, U-Boot boot-count rollback, a read-only root, and Podman app deployment
38 NixOS VM integration tests, including power-loss and watchdog-rollback scenarios, on Linux and macOS

projects.name: container-krun-runtime
projects.description: libkrun virtualization runtime for Apple's container; reclaims freed memory for macOS.
highlights: Feature parity for exec, volumes, virtio-fs, and port forwarding, plus memory the guest frees going back to macOS while it runs
Built a native vmnet virtio-net backend in libkrun (Rust) with packed rings, multiqueue TX, and batched syscalls

projects.name: container-compose-plugin
projects.description: Unmodified Docker Compose for Apple's container CLI.
highlights: Ports mirrored to localhost and a Docker socket for IDEs and Testcontainers
Built as an external plugin after Apple declined the upstream change

projects.name: HexBox
projects.description: On-demand ARM64 Linux Nix builder for nix-darwin, in Apple's container.
highlights: 27 releases to v1.2, with idle auto-shutdown and a persistent store
Weekly image rebuilds gated on a 7-day release age, and bot-driven dependency updates

projects.name: Open-source contributions
projects.description: Fixes in docker-library/python, mise, libkrun, and paho-mqtt.
highlights: docker-library/python (official image, 9B+ pulls): found and fixed a silent regression that skipped profile-guided optimization across 37 Dockerfile variants
jdx/mise: OS/architecture compound filters for tool installs
libkrun: released leaked vsock proxies after a clean guest shutdown
eclipse-paho/paho.mqtt.python, Himmelblau, and aube: reconnect and packaging fixes

contributions.text: released vsock proxies after a clean guest shutdown, so long-running hosts stop leaking them
kept arm64 release builds compatible with glibc 2.31, so they still run on older Debian and Ubuntu
added os/arch compound filters, so a tool can install on linux/arm64 only
added aarch64 packages for Debian-based distributions
fixed profile-guided optimization silently skipped across 37 variants of the official image
fixed a random crash on startup when the socket wasn't ready yet, so the client reconnects instead
